messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning: We need to respond with a JSON object containing the function call. The user wants to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. They provide version, IP, API name, and parameter. We have a function requests_get that takes url and fabricName. The URL template is "https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}". So we need to fill ip=192.168.11.33, fabricName=PEK-ACI. So URL becomes "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI". Then we call requests_get with that URL and fabricName. The function signature expects fabricName as separate param. So we pass fabricName: "PEK-ACI". The URL includes the placeholder replaced. So we produce JSON: {"name":"requests_get","arguments":{"url":"https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI","fabricName":"PEK-ACI"}}. That matches the function.
